findings.text: The synchronous initialization step inspects the pending queue and does nothing when it is empty or already led by a separator. When ordinary waiters are present it acquires a separator node and inserts it at the head, then publishes it as the wait tail with an exclusive-writer expectation and warns if a previous wait tail had not been consumed. If no separator is available it asks for another poll instead of proceeding. State involved includes srs_next and srs_wait_tail.

The synchronous cleanup step detaches the current wait tail and completes only ordinary waiter nodes up to a fixed per-pass bound, stopping early at the next separator or when the bound is reached, while keeping the tail link current. If only a trailing separator remains and no deferred cleanups are pending under acquire ordering, it releases that separator promptly. It then publishes the detached tail as the done tail with release ordering and, when work remains, raises a pending counter and queues background cleanup, compensating the counter if the queue request is already pending.

Grace initialization records activity, then under the root lock verifies that a start was requested and that no grace period is already active, clearing the request flags on success and returning a negative indication on spurious wakeup or overlap. Before advancing the global sequence it records stall-check timing, inserts the synchronous separator, snapshots the prior sequence, starts the new sequence, and announces the start. A separator shortage triggers an extra poll request after dropping the root lock.

During the offline and online reconciliation phase the initializer visits each leaf with interrupts disabled while holding hotplug exclusion and the leaf lock. When the baseline and next baseline agree and no blocked tasks are waiting, the leaf is skipped. Otherwise it applies the buffered baseline, initializes a newly online branch on first occupancy, retains a blocked-task wait when preempt-blocked tasks remain, and propagates a fully offline branch upward. A residual blocked wait is cleared when its tasks drain or the leaf regains online members, propagating upward when the leaf stays empty.

The breadth-first bring-up phase copies each node baseline need into the current need, publishes the new global sequence to the node, refreshes the local CPU view when the node owns the current CPU, arms the priority-boost window, and validates blocked-task state with an expectation that current need starts clear. For leaves with offline or blocked residual need it reports that need immediately while still holding the node lock; otherwise it releases the lock. Strict builds additionally broadcast a boundary notification, and the initializing CPU reports its own quiescent state under disabled preemption.

Grace initialization serializes start decisions with the root node lock held with interrupts disabled, then serializes each leaf reconciliation step with local interrupts disabled plus hotplug exclusion and the leaf node lock, and finally serializes each breadth-first node setup step with the corresponding node lock held with interrupts saved. The root sequence advance and flag manipulation occur only while the root lock is held, and per-node need and sequence publication occur only while that node lock is held.

The branch teardown and branch setup helpers require the leaf node lock already held with interrupts disabled. They walk toward the root acquiring each parent node lock in turn without re-enabling interrupts, update the parent baseline occupancy to clear or set the child contribution, and stop once a parent remains occupied or the root is passed. Teardown additionally expects an empty leaf baseline, no preempt-blocked tasks, and an empty current need at each visited parent.

Forced quiescent-state scans iterate leaves holding one leaf lock at a time with interrupts saved, probing outstanding members and either reporting collected need through a routine that consumes the lock or releasing the lock when nothing was collected. The single-shot forcing step clears its request flag under the root lock with interrupts disabled. Cleanup walks nodes breadth-first holding each node lock with interrupts disabled while validating emptiness, publishing the completed sequence, and extracting deferred-service state before releasing.

The global grace state progresses through distinct phases observed as idle, hotplug reconciliation, initialization, timed wait for forcing, active forcing, and back to idle. Initialization publishes reconciliation before node bring-up and then initialization; the forcing loop alternates timed wait and active forcing until completion; cleanup publishes idle only after all nodes have received the completed sequence.

The forcing loop wakes immediately on overload indication, on an explicit forcing request flag, or when the root shows no remaining need and no current-period blocked readers. It sleeps on a dedicated wait queue with a computed deadline, then either performs a forcing pass when the deadline expired or a request or overload is present, or treats the wakeup as stray and recomputes a shorter wait while preserving timing. The first forcing pass snapshots idle state and later passes recheck it; overload shortens subsequent waits.

The leaf scan refreshes a global overload latch from per-node overload indications, skips leaves with no current need except possibly initiating priority boost when blocked readers remain, and otherwise probes each outstanding member once. Positive probe outcomes are merged into a report mask that is reported under the leaf lock with urgency cleared, while negative outcomes are merged into a reschedule set that is kicked after the lock is released.

Each forcing pass records activity, increments a global force counter, and maintains a bounded stall-extension countdown that refreshes the stall deadline on its final use only when time advances. Afterwards it clears the explicit forcing request flag under the root lock so that a single request cannot cause immediate re-entry.

Cleanup records completion timing and maintains a maximum duration, closes the polled snapshot, derives a completed sequence value from the current global sequence, and publishes it to every node breadth-first. At each node it validates that no current-period blocked readers or residual need remain, refreshes the local CPU view when applicable, folds future-period cleanup need, re-evaluates per-member overload on leaves, and hands off deferred-service state for out-of-lock processing. The root sequence is then marked complete, the global state returns to idle, and need observed after the walk re-arms another period.

If the global sequence were advanced after scanning leaves for online members, a concurrently onlining CPU could be missed by the new period and its later reclamation could occur too early. The fragments therefore require sequence start before the hotplug scan and keep the root node sequence lagging the global sequence for single-node correctness.

Completing an unbounded number of synchronous waiters inside the grace thread could stall grace processing, so synchronous cleanup completes at most a fixed number per pass and defers any remainder plus separator reclamation to background work guarded by a pending counter. The fast release of a trailing separator is permitted only when an acquire read shows no background cleanups pending, preventing a separator from being dropped while workers still reference the chain.

The combining-tree node as observed carries current need, baseline need, and next baseline masks, plus a flag for waiting on blocked tasks, hierarchy linkage to a parent, a group mask, a CPU interval, and a level. It also carries a published sequence, a quiescent completion marker, blocked-task linkage with grace and boost and expedited anchors, an overload mask for members, a mask capturing initialization-time offline need, and a lock protecting these fields.

The global grace state as observed carries a name, a global sequence with a polled snapshot, request flags, activity and start timestamps, stall and forcing deadlines, a reschedule deadline, a bounded stall-extension counter, force counters with a start baseline, a maximum duration, an end timestamp, a phase indicator, a wait queue, tree storage, hotplug exclusion, overload latches, and a synchronous-wait subsystem with a pending list and a wait tail and a done tail and a pending cleanup counter and a cleanup work item.

Grace processing distinguishes separate named phases for idle, hotplug reconciliation, initialization, waiting for forced quiescent-state action, and performing forced quiescent-state action. The fragments treat these as distinct observable values of the global phase indicator.

Grace control distinguishes separate named request indications for explicit forcing and for overload-driven forcing, a named delay that offsets priority-boost arming from the current time, and a named bound that caps synchronous waiter completions per cleanup pass. The fragments treat these names as stable control parameters.

When preempt-blocked tracking is present, the per-node grace-start check warns on unexpected current-period blocked readers, anchors the grace-task pointer to the head of the blocked list and emits a trace event when tasks exist and the node is active, and expects empty current need. The boost starter arms a future deadline from the current time. Minimal builds reduce the check to an emptiness warning and the boost starter to a no-op and the blocked-task diagnostic to an assertion that the blocked list is empty, while the full diagnostic reports node sequences and masks and task anchors and list contents and per-member online and offline progress.

Stall supervision initialization captures the current time as the period start, derives a check interval, orders the start publication before stall and counter updates, zeroes the stall-extension allowance, computes stall and reschedule deadlines as offsets from the start, and snapshots the current force counter as the period baseline. The observed state includes start and stall deadline and extension allowance and reschedule deadline and force baseline.
